standalone.observation: Every named role carries its own one-line definition inline, including kayfabe itself, so a listener with no wrestling background can follow the whole piece without outside knowledge.

performer.observation: The Jobber persona is consistent and wry, self-deprecating about borrowed entrance music and twenty years of losing, and speaks directly to the front-row listener throughout.

storyBetweenCards.observation: The cards build a real night: roles, then selling tricks, then booking and camera tricks, then a real injury, the bell, the finish, and a retirement beat addressed to one audience member.

individuality.observation: Concrete details like the empty arena years and the real injury are specific to wrestling, but nearly every beat repeats the identical named-role-plus-one-line-definition shape, which flattens variety across the piece.

outro.observation: The line about choosing liars carefully closes the theme well, but the final sign-off reads as a stock tag with no earlier occurrence of that word anywhere else in the text.

transferable.observation: The named items (Babyface, Heel, Jobber, Leg Drop, Goldberg) are wrestling-specific terms that anchor the whole structure to this one subject.

flags.observation: First instance of the recurring pattern: "The Babyface: high-flying moves, because audiences cheer for that." sets a template repeated almost unchanged through many later beats.
"Never remove it." ends the card as a blunt command, a sharper and shorter stinger than the explanatory cadence used in neighboring beats.
"Goldberg's shoulder smashed into the ring-post." is the only beat naming a real, identifiable person, breaking from the otherwise generic archetype names.
"kicking out at two point nine nine, crowd vertical" packs a numeric detail and a fragment into one dense line, denser than the surrounding cards.
"You knew the ending, and you stood up at two point nine anyway." calls back to beat 29's near-fall count, tying the audience address to an earlier card.
"Stay Fluffy, Folks!" lands with no earlier occurrence of "Fluffy" anywhere in this text, so it reads as an outside tag rather than an earned payoff.
